authority: §R4c — an occurrence honestly judged NOT competent is recorded as a defect and LEFT FAILING; it is not registered to make the suite green
method: one judging agent per file reading the real source, then an independent adversarial agent per COMPETENT claim tasked with refuting it and defaulting to refuted when uncertain
consequence: these keys are deliberately NOT in gate_baseline.json, so ComposedGateTests::test_no_new_occurrences_outside_the_baseline continues to FAIL on exactly them

defects.claimed_justification: Every default here pushes toward the refusal. Line 137 register.get('candidates', []) -> len 0 -> `not (4 <= 0 <= 6)` -> CANDIDATE_COUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE -> FAIL. Line 143 ledger.get('entries', []) -> valid_ids empty -> every citation becomes CANDIDATE_CITES_UNKNOWN_ENTRY (over-fails, never under-fails). Line 157 c.get('inspired_by_ledger_entries', []) -> falsy -> CANDIDATE_CITES_NO_INSPIRATION. Line 175 is the authority-sensitive one and is the safe way round: mandate defaults to '', so `'OWNER_BLOCKER_CLEARANCE' in ''` is False, waived stays False and NO_QUIET_MINIMAL_CANDIDATE fires -- an absent or unreadable mandate can never silently waive the recorded C3-over-C1 owner taste; the waiver requires a positive substring match on real text. Lines 150/155/160/164 are _fail() detail strings only.
defects.refutation_reason: The COMPETENT claim is incomplete and its central mechanism is empirically false. The occurrence set for this key contains NINE lines, including line 152 `art = req / "candidates" / c.get(art_key, "__absent__")` — the one authority-bearing artifact check in the function — and the justification never mentions it. Lines 137/143/157/175 are traced correctly (I re-verified each: CANDIDATE_MIN=4 so an absent `candidates` key gives len 0 -> CANDIDATE_COUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE; empty `entries` over-fails via CANDIDATE_CITES_UNKNOWN_ENTRY; `mandate` defaulting to "" leaves `waived` False so NO_QUIET_MINIMAL_CANDIDATE stays enforced). But the file-level theory the claim rests on — the pattern quoted in competent pattern (a), ".get('file','') -> path -> not exists -> refusal" — DOES NOT HOLD in this function, because pathlib collapses a degenerate join: `Path(req)/"candidates"/""` returns the candidates DIRECTORY, and `.exists()` is True. Verified on this interpreter (3.9.6): `req/'candidates'/''` -> PosixPath('.../candidates'), exists=True. So the only structural check on the value looked up at line 152 is an existence test that a blank or degenerate value passes trivially. Competent pattern (c) also fails: the earlier check at lines 147-148 is `if k not in c` — PRESENCE ONLY. It does not guarantee the value is a usable filename, so nothing upstream constrains what line 152 hands to the path join. The result is a silently WRONG VERDICT on the stage whose own docstring promises "SVG and PNG both on disk", in a module whose header states "a stage that did not run is a visible FAIL, never a silent pass". Nothing downstream catches it: `request_summary` (lines 276-280) re-reports `png: c.get("png")` from the same register without any existence test, and `validate_request` ANDs the stage verdicts, so the whole request reports PASS. A blank-artifact register is exactly the shape a half-run or scaffolded generation step produces, i.e. the failure this validator exists to catch. Per the binding rule "if uncertain, judge NOT_COMPETENT", the strict caveat that the value flowing is a blank register field rather than the literal `"__absent__"` sentinel does not rescue the claim: the flagged construct is the substitute-instead-of-fail shape, and its asserted fail-closed consequence is the thing that is false here.
defects.counterexample: Live run of `validate_candidates` from apps/pipeline/services/h2_design_request.py against a request dir whose candidates/ contains ONLY candidate_register.json (zero SVGs, zero PNGs on disk), with a valid 2-entry ledger and a register of 4 candidates each shaped: {"candidate_id":"C0","title":"t","svg":"","png":"","inspired_by_ledger_entries":["E0"],"direction":"quiet_minimal","originality_statement":"s"}. Line 148 (`k not in c`) is satisfied because the keys are present; line 152 evaluates `req/"candidates"/""` which resolves to the existing candidates directory, so `art.exists()` is True and CANDIDATE_ARTIFACT_ABSENT NEVER FIRES. Actual returned record: {"stage":"candidates","findings":[],"verdict":"PASS","candidate_count":4} — files actually in candidates/: ['candidate_register.json']. A persisted count of 4 and a PASS verdict for "SVG and PNG both on disk" with zero artifacts on disk, no exception, no finding, and `request_summary` reporting the four candidates with blank png fields as fact. `"svg": "."` and any absolute path (e.g. "/etc/passwd") pass the same way.
defects.resolution: Repaired at 6602b40 under AO3(a)+(b). The artwork check now validates the candidate-supplied name as a plain filename BEFORE building a path (new code CANDIDATE_ARTIFACT_NAME_INVALID, deliberately distinct from CANDIDATE_ARTIFACT_ABSENT so 'you named nothing' and 'the file you named is gone' cannot be read as one defect), and tests is_file() rather than exists(), because a directory is not artwork. This entry's counterexample -- a register of four candidates with svg/png set to the empty string and zero files on disk, returning PASS with findings [] -- was re-run against the repair and now FAILS, as do '.', '..', a name containing a separator, and whitespace. The entry was RIGHT and its counterexample was better than the one found independently three days later by mutation; see AP for why it went unrepaired that long.

defects.finding: Weakest occurrence is line 238: `elif 'REJECT' in pick.get('verdict', '').upper()`. request_summary performs NO schema check on owner_pick_ingestion.json -- _load() (215-219) swallows OSError/ValueError and there is no validate_pick stage -- so a pick record that carries its decision under a different key is silently classified as NOT rejected and the stage advances to picked_awaiting_finalisation/accepted. This is not hypothetical: docs/roadmap/palt_h2/es3083_lid_alt_01/owner_pick_ingestion.json has NO 'verdict' key at all (its decision text lives in 'pick_verbatim'/'what_the_pick_authorizes'), so the branch is already being decided by the default rather than by evidence. The same absence propagates through lines 252-253 into the committed, drift-tested design_request_index.json, whose es3083 owner_pick_ingestion row is published with "verdict": "" and "verdict_verbatim": "" -- an owner decision rendered on /dashboard with an empty verdict cell, indistinguishable from a decision genuinely recorded as blank. The adjacent non-inventory branch at line 236 (`elif pick is None`) shows the same absence of any read-failure signal, since a corrupt pick file publishes 'awaiting_pick' and erases a real decision. Line 230 e.get('h2_request','').endswith(...) silently drops any emission lacking that key from the request, removing an owner acceptance from owner_decisions and regressing stage. Lines 261/265/266 do the same for acceptance authority/verbatim/date, and 270/273 stamp '?' into published product and tier fields.
defects.downstream_effect: CONFIRMED LIVE in the committed index: for es3083_lid_alt_01 the line-238 branch is decided by the '' default rather than by any recorded verdict (that record has no 'verdict' key), and design_request_index.json -- committed, drift-tested, and served to the dashboard by h2_views.py -- publishes that owner decision with "verdict": "" and "verdict_verbatim": "". LATENT, not yet observed: es3083's published stage 'accepted' happens to be correct because the pick was in fact an accept, but a pick of the same shape whose rejection is recorded under 'pick_verbatim' would be classified not-rejected and published as stage 'picked_awaiting_finalisation'/'accepted' -- a wrong verdict with nothing to catch it.
defects.resolution: Repaired at 6602b40. The pick verdict is no longer read through a defaulted lookup: the decision dialect is resolved explicitly and recorded on the row, and _list_field replaces the defaulted collection reads by distinguishing three states the empty-list default merged -- record absent, field absent, and field present but not a list -- surfacing them as record_defects rather than as a count of zero. The live harm this entry named is discharged in the committed artefact: design_request_index.json now publishes verdict 'A2 Twelve-Rosette' and decision_dialect pick_verbatim_field for es3083_lid_alt_01, where it previously published the empty string twice.

defects.finding: This key is the lookup_default set plus the collection defaults, and is judged by the same weakest occurrence, line 238, whose '' default silently reclassifies a pick record with no 'verdict' key as not-rejected (proven live on es3083_lid_alt_01, which has no such key). The collection defaults add a second, numeric instance of the defect: line 275 len((ledger or {}).get('entries', [])) combines with _load()'s except-swallow at 215-219, so an unreadable or malformed inspiration_ledger.json publishes ledger_entries: 0 as asserted fact regardless of register state, with nothing anywhere recording that the file could not be read; additionally, when the candidate register is also absent, the stage collapses to 'brief' instead of 'harvest' at line 233. Line 229 (emission_record or {}).get('emissions', []) does the same for the emission record: an unreadable m7_ai_emission_record.json yields emissions [], which drives stage back to 'picked_awaiting_finalisation' and empties the emissions and owner_decisions lists for a request that was in fact emitted and accepted. Line 274/280 propagate the same silence into brief_measurement_tiers and the candidates list.
defects.downstream_effect: The committed h2_design_request_index/1.0 record and the dashboard it feeds can publish a wrong stage, a wrong ledger_entries count of 0, and a missing owner acceptance whenever a source file is unreadable or uses a different key -- and the index's own staleness test (test_h2_design_request.py:52-60) compares the committed file against design_request_index() computed by the same defaulting code, so it detects staleness but never substitution.
defects.resolution: Repaired at 6602b40, same weakest occurrence as the lookup_default entry above and the same repair; recorded separately because the key names the detector shape rather than the line, which is the finding AP was written about. The collection defaults this entry additionally named are gone too: ledger_entries is computed from _list_field, and the emission record is read by _emissions_for, which refuses a malformed emissions block outright instead of yielding an empty list that silently regressed a request's published stage.

defects.finding: JUDGED BY ITS WEAKEST OCCURRENCES, 262 and 265 — the two occurrences this key holds that the lookup_default key does not (which is why the two keys diverge). Line 262 `mode_a = manifest.get("modes", {}).get(MODE_GEOMETRY_VALIDATION, {})` and line 265 `for view, rec in sorted(mode_a.get("views", {}).items())`: when the mode-A block exists but carries no `views` map (or an empty one), the verification loop body never executes, `findings` stays empty, and the function RETURNS SUCCESSFULLY at 289 with `views: {}` — the docstring's promise that EVERY referenced view is re-proved against the render evidence becomes vacuously true over zero views. Nothing downstream catches it: review_package's §1 mode guard at 462-465 does not fire because `mode_block` is truthy (the block exists, it just has no views); `_assert_provenance_complete` passes because `inputs_read_in_order` is still non-empty from the manifest (283) and contact-sheet (286) entries; and the injected provider in management/commands/rbv4_review.py:203-206 walks TRANSMITTED_VIEWS with `if path:` and silently skips every one. The other occurrences in this key are fail-closed and would be COMPETENT alone: 254/255 default `sheet.get("file","")` to the package directory itself, os.path.isfile is False, RBV4_CONTACT_SHEET_MISSING is appended and raised at 280-281; 263/266 default the view path to a directory, giving RBV4_VIEW_MISSING, and any path that does resolve is still compared to the recorded decoded-pixel hash at 272 (RBV4_VIEW_HASH_MISMATCH).
defects.downstream_effect: A persisted claude_visual_review_record.json is emitted disposing all 14 contract-required categories (silhouette, shoulder, neck, closure, proportion, perspective, artwork/logo placement, typography, material, lighting, colour, presentability, uncertainty) with ZERO geometry views hash-verified and, on the live path, only the contact sheet transmitted — a review record that reads to the owner as hash-verified geometry evidence while no view file was ever proved or looked at, with no code emitting any absence.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change. load_review_package now REQUIRES contact_sheet.file and contact_sheet.pixel_hash, and per view source_file and pixel_hash, raising RBV4_PACKAGE_SCHEMA_MISMATCH naming the missing field. The degenerate join this entry relied on -- joining a package directory to the empty string yields the DIRECTORY -- is unreachable, and the second, quieter half is closed too: an undeclared sheet used to be reported as CONTACT_SHEET_MISSING with no name, sending a reviewer to look for a sheet nobody ever declared, and a hash comparison against None could never say what it expected. RBV-3 writes both fields unconditionally, so the requirement refuses only manifests RBV-3 did not write.

defects.finding: JUDGED BY ITS WEAKEST OCCURRENCE, 528 `"provider_request_id": identity.get("request_id", "")`. The live branch validates two fields of the SAME identity dict with an explicit refusal — `if not identity.get("name") or not identity.get("model")` raises RBV4_PROVIDER_IDENTITY_INCOMPLETE at 513-515 — and then silently defaults the third. The provider is caller-injected (508-511), so a provider returning name+model without a request id produces a record whose execution block reads `"state": "EXECUTED"`, `"provider_call_made": true` and `"provider_request_id": ""` — the field this file's own comment at 526-527 calls "the audit link back to the committed ledger row: this record and the spend it caused name each other". `_assert_provenance_complete` (671-673) checks only `response_sha256` for the live path, so nothing refuses, and the record is written to disk at 587-590. That this identity can be lost is documented in this programme's own committed evidence: docs/visual_quality/rbv/rbv4_call_budget.json line 19 records a real ledger row as `"provider_request_id": "IDENTITY_LOST_TO_AN_EXECUTOR_DEFECT"`. The in-repo command does pass a ledgered id (commands/rbv4_review.py:146-147,166, and append_ledger_entry at 427-431 refuses a falsy provider_request_id with RBV4_LEDGER_ENTRY_INCOMPLETE) — but that guarantee lives in the CALLER, not in this harness, and cost_ledger.provider_request_id returns the sentinel PROVIDER_REQUEST_ID_NOT_RETURNED rather than "" precisely because blanks were judged dishonest elsewhere. Occurrence 546 `manifest.get("statement", "")` alone would be COMPETENT: it is prose copied into the record for display and is read by no count, disposition or gate.
defects.downstream_effect: A committed evidence record asserting that one of the ten owner-authorized §R1 provider calls was spent, with the identifier that would tie it to a row of rbv4_call_budget.json silently blank — the §R1a spend accounting loses its record↔ledger correspondence and the owner reading the record under §R4 cannot verify which ledgered call, if any, produced these dispositions.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change. provider_request_id and statement are read by subscript from a manifest the loader has already validated, so an absent field is a refusal rather than an empty string copied into a committed owner-facing review record as though the provider had returned nothing. The mode refusal was also split: 'you asked for the wrong mode' and 'this package does not declare that mode' were fused into one boolean arriving with reasons UNKNOWN, and are now two states, one of which names the manifest's own recorded reason.

defects.finding: JUDGED BY ITS WEAKEST OCCURRENCE, 528, identically to review_package|lookup_default: `identity.get("request_id", "")` defaults the audit link on a record stamped EXECUTED, while `name` and `model` from the same dict are refused when absent (RBV4_PROVIDER_IDENTITY_INCOMPLETE, 513-515) and `_assert_provenance_complete` never checks the request id. The other two occurrences are sound: 462 `mode_block = manifest.get("modes", {}).get(mode)` has NO default on the inner get, so an absent mode yields None and the §1 two-mode guard at 463-465 raises RBV4_MODE_ABSENT with its reasons — the `{}` default only routes to that refusal; 546 is display-only prose. The key is judged by 528.
defects.downstream_effect: Same as the lookup_default key: a persisted live-execution record whose provider_request_id is blank, unmatchable against the committed call ledger, with the harness reporting no defect — the failure mode already recorded once in rbv4_call_budget.json as IDENTITY_LOST_TO_AN_EXECUTOR_DEFECT.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change, same repair as the lookup_default entry above; separate only because the key names a detector shape. Recorded here rather than folded in, because folding two shapes of one occurrence into one entry is how the register lost sight of the h2 fail-open for three days (see AP).

defects.finding: JUDGED BY ITS WEAKEST OCCURRENCE, 401 `"authorizing_ruling": budget.get("authorized_by", "")`. This is the citation naming the owner ruling under which provider spend is authorized, and it is PERSISTED: docs/visual_quality/rbv/review_records/p1_v4/claude_visual_review_record.json:37 carries it as "PROJECT_OWNER — OWNER_BLOCKER_CLEARANCE.md §R1, 2026-08-17". If the committed budget ever lacks `authorized_by`, budget_state returns an empty citation, review_package embeds that block into the record at 532, and the record is written with an authority line that is blank and unrefused. The asymmetry inside the same record makes the defect concrete: line 552 takes `live_contract["authority_rules"]` by DIRECT INDEX (KeyError on absence), while the budget's authority citation defaults to "" — same authority class, opposite failure modes, in the same assembled record. No consumer reads the field today (grep finds it only in the committed record itself), which is exactly why a blank would go unnoticed. The other two occurrences are individually fail-closed and would be COMPETENT alone: 393 `int(budget.get("authorized_calls", 0))` defaults to the CONSERVATIVE value — 0 authorized forces remaining=0 at 395 and BUDGET_EXHAUSTED at 396, so review_package raises RBV4_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (504-507) and review_with_budget degrades to the fixture path stamped RECORDED_FIXTURE; it can never authorize a call the committed record did not (and append_ledger_entry at 432 indexes `budget["authorized_calls"]` directly, hard-failing on the write path). 402 `bool(budget.get("rollover", False))` defaults to the no-rollover reading and is consumed by no logic in this module.
defects.downstream_effect: A committed review record reporting a spent, owner-budgeted provider call whose authorizing ruling is recorded as the empty string — the §R1 authority citation on the evidence the owner reads at clearance is silently blank rather than refused, in a record where the contract's own authority rules would have raised KeyError under the same condition.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change. load_budget requires rollover to be PRESENT and boolean -- a truthiness test would have refused every honest record, since false is a legitimate value -- and budget_state reads authorized_calls, authorized_by and rollover by subscript. The harm was concrete: rollover is persisted into the committed claude_visual_review_record.json, so defaulting it wrote 'this budget does not roll over' into an owner-facing record on the authority of a record that said nothing. R1b makes False correct for this budget; a default that is right by coincidence is still a fabricated claim about the next one.

defects.finding: Same three occurrences as budget_state|lookup_default and judged by the same weakest one, 401 `budget.get("authorized_by", "")` — the owner-ruling citation for provider spend, defaulted to "" and then persisted into the review record via the `budget` block at line 532/403, unrefused, while the contract's authority_rules on the same record are taken by direct index at 552 and would raise. 393's default 0 is the fail-closed value (drives BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and refusal of the live path at 504-507, never an extra authorized call) and 402's default False is the no-rollover reading consumed by nothing; neither would fail on its own, but the key is judged by 401.
defects.downstream_effect: Identical to the lookup_default key: the persisted §R1 authorization citation on committed review evidence can be silently empty, and no code path reports its absence.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change, same occurrences and same repair as the budget_state lookup_default entry above; recorded separately because the key names the detector shape and not the line. Both shapes are now absent from the function.

defects.finding: Judged by its weakest occurrence, line 234: `expected = manifest.get("pixel_hashes", {}).get(view)` followed by `if expected and pixel_hash(path) != expected`. When the key (or one view's entry) is absent, `expected` is None, the `and` short-circuits, and the decoded-pixel verification that is this module's entire stated guarantee is SKIPPED — any file sitting under the recorded name is admitted and returned as verified. PROVEN, not inferred: I staged the committed V4 evidence with the front render overwritten by the top render. With `pixel_hashes` present the load REFUSES with `RBV3_VIEW_HASH_MISMATCH:front:neutral_front.png`; with `pixel_hashes` removed from the manifest the identical swap is ACCEPTED as 8 verified views. The default is precisely what converts a refusal into a pass. Line 228 (`manifest.get("views", {})`) is the second fail-open: default `{}` means the verification loop never executes, no finding is appended, and the function returns success with `resolved_views == {}` — also proven against a staged manifest. Competent pattern (c) does NOT apply here and must not be claimed: line 224 checks one self-declared schema STRING and zero keys — both staged manifests declared `geometry_validation_render_manifest/1.0` and still passed. The path is reachable because `render_dir` is an arbitrary caller-supplied directory and real evidence demonstrably drifts from the renderer's current output — the committed V4 tree already required four rebindings (front→neutral_front.png etc). Line 229 alone would be competent (falling back to the recorded name is the designed opt-in rebinding semantics, and a wrong file is still caught whenever hashes exist) but cannot carry the key.
defects.downstream_effect: A render directory whose manifest lacks `pixel_hashes` (or lacks one view's entry) yields a package whose manifest records `"pixel_hash"` values from an unverified file, and `build_review_package` then persists it and composes the contact sheet from renders that were never checked — the reviewer forms a geometry verdict on images the module claims, in its own docstring and manifest, to have hash-verified. A manifest lacking `views` yields a committed review package with zero renders, an empty `views` block, a contact sheet with no view panels, and no refusal anywhere: `build_review_package` iterates the empty dict at line 424 and skips the bounds view at line 451.
defects.resolution: OVERTURNED on re-judgment 2026-08-20. The entry was RIGHT about the occurrence it named -- the defaulted two-step lookup into `pixel_hashes`, which let a view with no recorded hash skip the decoded-pixel comparison and be returned as verified -- and that occurrence is repaired: the hash is required and the comparison is unconditional. The expression that survives under this coarse key is a different one, the optional view-rebinding map, and it was re-refuted from scratch and judged COMPETENT; see the registration in gate_baseline.json. The entry is kept, not deleted, because a register that forgets a defect cannot show that the judgment which found it was correct -- and this one was.

defects.finding: Judged by its weakest occurrence, line 361: `warnings = manifest.get("warnings", [])`. Line 362 then draws `"warnings: " + (", ".join(warnings) if warnings else "none")`. An ABSENT or renamed key is therefore rendered on the review sheet as the positive assertion `warnings: none`, and the colour expression at 369-370 (`not line.startswith("warnings") or not warnings`) evaluates True on the empty list, so it is drawn in grey (60,60,64) rather than the red reserved for real warnings. A missing key is presented to the reviewer as a clean bill of health, which is the defect class exactly: the committed subject genuinely carries `["RENDER_OFF_CENTER:closure_detail"]`, and the honest red display of that code is the documented purpose of this block. Line 346 (`dims = manifest.get("dimensions", {})`) is the second weak occurrence, with two distinct failure modes on the same loosely-fetched dict: (i) default `{}` makes `if dims:` false at 348, so the CONTRACT DIMENSIONS restatement is silently omitted — and that restatement exists precisely because §S2 measured the renderer-baked annotations in `bounds_dimensions` as illegible after the provider downscale, so its omission leaves illegible text as the ONLY dimension figures on the sheet, while line 402 still records a `contract_dimensions` legibility entry for the placeholder string never drawn; (ii) line 352's `dims.get('side_depth_mm') or dims.get('front_width_mm')` prints the FRONT WIDTH under a `D` label whenever `side_depth_mm` is absent or 0 — a wrong number presented as a measured contract dimension, invisible in the committed evidence only because this subject happens to have W == D == 37.4mm. The remaining occurrences are weaker findings and I say so rather than inflating them: 340 (`measurements`) renders a visible `expected_mm_per_px: None` and an empty §11 block — an obvious absence, not a false figure; 303 (`reference_availability`) yields a blank banner — omission, not a false claim; 299 is charged under the lookup_default key; 387/388 are provenance strings that degrade to blank, never to a wrong engine name.
defects.downstream_effect: A render manifest missing `warnings` produces a contact sheet that tells the RBV-4 provider and the owner, in non-alarming grey, that the render passed §11 with no warnings — the geometry verdict is then formed against a suppressed defect list. A manifest missing `dimensions`, or carrying a dimensions block without `side_depth_mm`, produces either a sheet with no legible contract dimensions at all (with a legibility record claiming otherwise) or a sheet stating a depth equal to the front width.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change. `warnings` is in REQUIRED_RENDER_MANIFEST_LISTS, so load_validation_render refuses a manifest that omits it, and _compose_sheet now reads `manifest['warnings']` by subscript at line 458. The entry's harm is discharged exactly as it was stated: the sheet can no longer draw `warnings: none` -- a POSITIVE ASSERTION that the render carried no warnings -- on the authority of a manifest that never mentioned warnings at all, and it can no longer draw that assertion in the non-alerting colour. The distinction the entry turned on is preserved in the repair rather than flattened by it: `warnings: []` is still legal and still renders `none`, because a measured empty list IS the claim that there were no warnings. Absent and empty were the two states the default merged.

defects.finding: Judged by its weakest occurrence, line 299: `manifest.get("statement", "")` is banners[0], the FIRST line under the sheet title and the only banner drawn in red (line 308, `fill=red if i == 0`). In the committed evidence that field reads `GEOMETRY VALIDATION FIXTURE — NOT A REAL BOTTLE COMPARISON`. The claim here is not that the default writes a wrong value — a blank cannot assert a false caveat — it is narrower and still disqualifying: the §1 two-mode caveat that CONSTRAINS what these renders may be read as vanishes from the artifact the reviewer actually looks at, nothing in this module asserts the field non-empty, and a validation render presented with no fixture caveat is exactly the re-badging the two-mode rule exists to forbid. Line 303 (`reference_availability`) is a weaker occurrence and I record it as such: a blank `reference availability: ` banner withholds information rather than misstating it. Lines 387/388 (`blender_version`, `render_engine`) would be COMPETENT standing alone — they are display-only provenance in the footer, they degrade to blank rather than naming a wrong engine, and the non-defaulted `render['manifest_sha256']` printed on the same line pins the source manifest exactly, so any reader can recover the true engine — but a key is judged by its weakest member, and 299 is not display-only in the exculpating sense: the banner's content is what governs how the images beneath it may be interpreted.
defects.downstream_effect: The contact sheet — the single artifact transmitted to the reviewing provider and shown to the owner — loses the red 'GEOMETRY VALIDATION FIXTURE / NOT A REAL BOTTLE COMPARISON' line, so neutral clay validation renders reach a geometry verdict with no statement of what they are and are not, while the package still passes every check in this module.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change, same function and same repair boundary as the regex entry above; recorded separately because the key names the detector shape and not the line, which is the finding AP was written about. `statement` is required by load_validation_render and read by subscript at line 389. The entry was careful that the default writes no FALSE caveat -- a blank cannot assert one -- and narrower: it silently drops the red banner a human reviewer is meant to read first, so a fixture sheet and a real comparison sheet became indistinguishable at a glance. That is closed at the boundary now, not by argument about whether the banner matters.

defects.finding: Judged by its weakest occurrence, line 483: `"warnings": manifest.get("warnings", [])` writes the default straight into the COMMITTED package manifest under `modes.GEOMETRY_VALIDATION.warnings`, where it is no longer transient. The dashboard renders that field at templates/dashboard/rbv3_review_packages.html line 37 as `{{ ...warnings|join:", "|default:"none" }}` inside the red `warn` cell, so a missing upstream key becomes the literal owner-facing string `none` under the heading '§11 warnings' — a persisted, displayed assertion that the render raised no findings, produced by a key that was simply absent. Line 484 (`uncertainty`, default `[]`) is equally weak: the committed subject declares `["V3 provisional geometry — owner review pending"]`, and an absent key persists an empty list that reads as 'no uncertainty declared' on a package whose whole purpose is honest qualification. Weaker occurrences, stated as such rather than inflated: 482 (`measurements`, default `{}`) persists a visibly empty block rather than a wrong figure, and 463/486 are charged under the lookup_default key for this symbol. Nothing between these lines and `json.dump` at 504 inspects the values — the only fail-closed check in this function (445) tests sheet legibility, not manifest completeness.
defects.downstream_effect: A package manifest is committed and served that states, on the owner's dashboard review surface, that the render carried no §11 warnings and declared no uncertainty. defects.claimed_justification: Line 394, `("banner", banners[0] or "statement", 28)`, supplies the SAMPLE TEXT for the `banner` role passed to `sheet_legibility`, which feeds the §S2 fail-closed gate at line 445. The substitute is the SMALLER, i.e. strictly more conservative, sample — it cannot inflate `effective_px` and so cannot let the `below_floor` check pass a size it would otherwise fail. The genuinely load-bearing input to that gate is the font size, and it is the literal `28` here, matching the literal `28` actually used at line 307; it is not defaulted. The substitution also fires only when `banners[0]` is empty, i.e. when no banner text was drawn at all, so it cannot misjudge any text a reviewer will see. Finally, sample substitution is the module's design throughout this call, not an evasion introduced here — seven of the ten roles pass hardcoded representative strings (`"expected_mm_per_px: 0.05819"`, `"source: RBV-2B manifest sha256 0123456789abcdef"`), because the record audits the composer's font sizing, not the sheet's wording. The harm of an empty statement is real but belongs to lines 299 and 463, where I have charged it NOT_COMPETENT; it must not be double-counted here, and an empty banner is a missing-text defect, not an illegible-text defect, so this gate is not the mechanism that should catch it.
defects.refutation_reason: The claimed justification measures the right thing against the wrong baseline. `or` fires ONLY when `banners[0]` is falsy, i.e. only when the statement is empty/absent — so the case it compares against (a present statement at 21px) is exactly the case in which the substitution never happens. The true counterfactual is `"statement"` vs `""`. Measured directly with the module's own `_glyph_px` and its pinned font `/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc`: `_glyph_px("", 28) == 0` (textbbox `(0,0,0,0)`), `_glyph_px("statement", 28) == 20`. At the real sheet's downscale (long edge 3840, factor 0.6708) that is 0.0px vs 13.42px across a floor of `SHEET_TEXT_MIN_EFFECTIVE_PX = 12.0`. The default therefore does the precise thing the justification says it cannot: it carries the `banner` role across the §S2 floor, converting a fail-closed refusal into a pass. (1) THE GATE FLIP. Confirmed end-to-end against the real committed evidence: I copied `docs/visual_quality/rbv/p1_pilot/2026-08-04_v4` and changed one field, `statement` -> `""`. `build_review_package(...)` returned NORMALLY with `below_floor: []`, `worst_effective_px: 13.42`, and wrote `review_package_manifest.json`. With the same input and the `banner` sample left as the real empty `banners[0]`, the identical run raised `Rbv3Refusal(['RBV3_SHEET_TEXT_ILLEGIBLE:banner:0.0px<12.0'])` at line 445. Nothing upstream constrains the field: `load_validation_render` validates only `manifest["schema"]` and the per-view decoded-pixel hashes, and editing `statement` leaves every view hash valid — so "hash-verified manifest" does not make this key structurally guaranteed. (2) THE PERSISTED FALSE NUMBER. The returned dict is stored at line 495 as `"legibility": legibility` in the committed, owner-facing package manifest, recording `texts[banner] = {font_size: 28, glyph_px: 20, effective_px: 13.42}` and a headline `worst_effective_px: 13.42` for a line that the composer drew as the empty string — I cropped the generated sheet's banner band (y 125-175) and it is background pixels only. That falsifies the function's own stated contract, `sheet_legibility` docstring lines 151-152: "Nothing here asserts legibility — every number is a measurement of the text that will actually be transmitted." Here the number is a measurement of a string that was never transmitted. (3) WHAT THE MISSING TEXT IS. `banners[0]` is `manifest["statement"]`, which for this generator is `NOT_REAL_BOTTLE` = "GEOMETRY VALIDATION FIXTURE — NOT A REAL BOTTLE COMPARISON" — the §1 disclaimer that stops a reviewer reading a validation render as a real product. Its total absence from the sheet is certified in the manifest as legible at 13.42px. ON THE DOUBLE-COUNTING DEFENCE: lines 299/463 propagate the empty statement into the drawn sheet and into `package["statement"]`; line 394 does something additional and PRIOR — it suppresses the refusal that would have stopped the package being written at all, since the raise at 445 precedes the `json.dump` at 504. Remove 394's default and 299/463's harm never ships. It is the gating occurrence, not a duplicate. ON "the refusal code would be mislabelled": the gate is fail-closed and 0px is the honest measurement of the text that will actually be transmitted; arguing the code name should differ is a gate-weakening argument and out of scope under the rules of evidence.

defects.claimed_justification: Both defaults were checked in the PASS direction by execution, not by reading. (1) max_profile_deviation=PROFILE_DEVIATION_THRESHOLD=0.05 decides `within` at line 269 and the aspect axis at line 280, but the measured instrument noise floor is 0.1359 (canonical_self_comparison, run against this working tree), i.e. the default is 2.7x TIGHTER than the instrument can resolve — it cannot manufacture an unearned PASS; a subject that IS the canonical still records FAIL/RBV5_PROFILE_DIVERGENT, which the suite pins (test_the_gate_reports_fail_rather_than_widening, and test_self_comparison_measures_instrument_noise asserts noise > threshold). The number is persisted at record['thresholds']['profile_max_abs_deviation'] with status PROVISIONAL_PENDING_OWNER_CALIBRATION, so no reader can mistake it for a calibrated value. (2) ratio=1.0 selects the basis, and 1.0 is the only self-consistent value: ratio=1.4 REFUSES at the normalisation assertion (RBV5_PROFILE_NORMALISATION_UNVERIFIED:basis:peak=1.4) and ratio=0.7 worsens deviation 0.1359 -> 0.3001. Every departure from the default either refuses or tightens; widening the basis to fit a distorted subject is impossible. CAVEAT for the owner: the effective ratio is NOT written into the emitted record (verified: only 'contrast_ratio' matches), so a non-default ratio is not auditable from the record alone — a disclosure gap on an explicitly-passed argument, not a defect of the default.
defects.refutation_reason: The certification's load-bearing sentence ("the default is 2.7x TIGHTER than the instrument can resolve - it cannot manufacture an unearned PASS") measures the PROFILE axis floor only (0.1359). The same default governs a SECOND axis, body_aspect_h_over_w (lines 280/283), and that axis's floor, taken from the module's own canonical_self_comparison(), is |3.0172 - 3.0606| = 0.0434 < 0.05. On that axis the default sits ABOVE the noise floor and does grant PASS. The default-specific defect is the band: the PASS band is 0-0.05 while the instrument's own aspect noise is 0.0434, so ~87% of the band is noise and every PASS on this axis is noise-determined, not geometry-determined. That matters because the profile axis CANNOT detect proportion distortion at all - both sides are max-width-normalised (measure_mask / sample_geometry divide by max half-width), so a uniform x-distortion cancels identically; measured profile deviation is flat ~0.134-0.142 across every distortion I rendered. body_aspect_h_over_w is therefore the ONLY axis in the entire gate that can catch the distortion class M3 calibration exists for, and it is the one the default silently governs. Nothing catches or flags it: the aspect axis's reason string states no criterion (the profile axis prints "0.1359 > 0.05"; the aspect axis prints only subject/canonical/delta); the record's sole persisted threshold is named thresholds.profile_max_abs_deviation, attributing the number to the profile, so an owner cannot see it decided aspect; no test touches it (test_self_comparison_measures_instrument_noise asserts only the PROFILE max_abs_deviation > threshold, test_the_gate_reports_fail_rather_than_widening pins the PROFILE axis, and no test measures the aspect noise floor or asserts the aspect verdict); and GEOMETRY's verdict reason reads "1 axis/axes measured and did not satisfy the criterion", affirmatively implying the other three measured axes DID satisfy it. Yes, gate_state is FAIL regardless - but the task's defect class names "a measurement, a verdict, a persisted number, or a report an owner would read as fact", and body_aspect_h_over_w: PASS with measured.delta is all four in the emitted record, whose own thresholds.note casts it as the owner's calibration evidence. One knob, two axes with floors 3x apart: the calibration the record invites (raise the threshold past the 0.1359 profile floor) drags the aspect tolerance from 0.05 to >0.1359, which by the measured table passes distortion beyond ratio 0.95. Secondary: ratio is absent from the record entirely (only "contrast_ratio" matches; basis.m3_canonical = canonical_bounds() is ratio-independent with no distortion_ratio key), so a reader cannot even confirm the default basis was the one used.
defects.counterexample: Executed in the repo venv against this working tree, calling compare(subject, basis=BASIS_M3_CANONICAL, ...) with BOTH defaults (ratio=1.0, max_profile_deviation=0.05). Subject = extract_mask(m3.render_sample(r)) -> measure_mask. Results for body_aspect_h_over_w: r=1.000 PASS delta 0.0434 | r=0.990 PASS delta 0.0171 | r=0.986 PASS delta 0.0038 | r=0.980 PASS delta 0.0096 | r=0.970 FAIL delta 0.0505 | r=0.950 FAIL delta 0.1068 (profile axis FAIL at 0.134-0.142 throughout, carrying no distortion signal). THE COUNTEREXAMPLE: a subject rendered at horizontal distortion ratio 0.986 - genuinely NOT the canonical, 1.4% narrower - emits the persisted axis record body_aspect_h_over_w: state PASS, reason "subject 3.0568 vs canonical 3.0606 (delta 0.0038)", measured {subject: 3.0568, basis: 3.0606, delta: 0.0038}. The record thus affirms a near-exact proportion match for a distorted subject, while the TRUE canonical subject records delta 0.0434 - eleven times worse. Over 0.98-1.00 the axis is inverted (more distorted reads as better match) because the instrument's -0.0434 aspect bias cancels the distortion, and the default threshold converts that noise into an affirmative PASS verdict. No refusal is raised, no code is attached, no criterion is printed, and the only threshold the record discloses is labelled as belonging to the profile.
defects.resolution: Repaired in the commit carrying this register change. compare()'s ratio is now REQUIRED and basis.ratio carries it into the record. The case for the old default was the strongest of the sixteen -- 1.0 is the identity of a multiplicative scale, not a stand-in for a measurement nobody took, and omitting it produced a false FAIL rather than a false PASS -- and it was required anyway, for a reason the identity argument does not reach: THE RECORD DID NOT SAY WHICH RATIO IT USED, so a record produced against a defaulted basis and one produced against a chosen basis were indistinguishable to any reader. A default is tolerable only when the output states that it fired. NOTE, recorded against this entry: its argument that max_profile_deviation also governs body_aspect_h_over_w was true once and is not true now (sprint 3 split the constants), and it named an expression whose default is a Name, which this detector shape does not flag -- the entry was right about the key and wrong about the line.

So a "cost that will not parse" is NOT converted into an RBV4_LEDGER_ENTRY_UNKNOWN_WITHOUT_DEFECT finding — and because the escape unwinds `validate_ledger_row` before `if findings: raise Rbv4Refusal(findings)`, it DESTROYS every finding already collected on that row (placeholder request id, zero input tokens, non-int output tokens).
